candidate.blueprint_locator: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — medication administration, contraindications/precautions, and monitoring
candidate.blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — stimulant cardiac safety
candidate.educational_objective: Identify when a cardiac history requires clarification before initiating stimulant therapy.

options.A: Administer the dose because stimulants improve cardiac function
options.B: Ignore the history because stimulants do not affect heart rate or blood pressure
options.C: Permanently stop all future ADHD treatment because any past arrhythmia is an absolute contraindication
options.D: Clarify the cardiac history and prescription with the prescriber before administration

candidate.rationale: Current methylphenidate labeling warns against use in patients with serious cardiac disease, including serious cardiac arrhythmia, and states that CNS stimulants increase blood pressure and heart rate. A newly identified arrhythmia therefore requires prescriber clarification and individualized assessment before the first dose. The label does not make every past arrhythmia an automatic permanent contraindication to all ADHD treatment. D is correct.
candidate.source_claim_supported: CNS stimulants can increase blood pressure and heart rate; methylphenidate labeling advises avoiding use in serious cardiac disease including serious cardiac arrhythmia.
candidate.source_locator: Warnings and Precautions 5.2 Risks to Patients with Serious Cardiac Disease; 5.3 Increased Blood Pressure and Heart Rate
candidate.source_organization: DailyMed / U.S. National Library of Medicine (official FDA drug labeling)
candidate.stem: Before the first dose of a newly prescribed CNS stimulant, a nurse discovers a documented cardiac arrhythmia that may not have been considered when the prescription was written. What is the safest action?
